title: Unified Inverse-Walk Mixing Bound
summary: Characteristic-specific comparison methods are available, but a common upper-bound proof for the inverse walk across both regimes remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Develop a unified proof of the inverse-walk upper mixing bound over finite fields that applies in both odd characteristic and characteristic $2$. The existing odd-characteristic strategy produces $3$-cycles by first constructing a three-term arithmetic progression, but that intermediate construction has no counterpart in characteristic $2$; the unresolved task is therefore to obtain one upper-bound argument that works in both regimes.

scope.domain: Probability and algebraic structures of inverse walks over finite fields.
parameters: Finite fields with characteristic either odd or 2, defining the two regimes the unified bound must cover
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether a common upper-bound approach exists and, if so, develop a proof that applies in both odd characteristic and characteristic 2.

citations.label: How Fast Does the Inverse Walk Approximate a Random Permutation?

progress.summary: The source presents the issue as a common upper-bound question, noting that the odd-characteristic 3-cycle construction does not immediately transfer to characteristic 2.
citation_labels: Vishesh Jain et al., How Fast Does the Inverse Walk Approximate a Random Permutation?
